videos.title: Money Lessons From Americans Caring for Aging Parents | Life Lessons | Business Insider
videos.how_counted: Hand tally of top-level threads and replies in which the writer describes their own or their immediate family's caregiving; one comment can count toward several themes. Approximate (+/- 15%). Roughly 190 of 278 threads are praise, advice, ads (a financial-advisor sponsor was named and mocked), political argument, tributes, or opinions about whether adult children owe care.
videos.audience_note: A money-themed, sponsor-presented news video. Commenters split between (a) caregivers describing cost shock (assisted living and memory care quoted at $5k to $12k per month, Medicaid and spend-down, parents with no savings), lost jobs, uneven sibling help, and parents they resent, and (b) a large group of non-caregivers arguing about saving, long-term-care insurance, financial planners, euthanasia, moving abroad, and whether children owe care. Topic skews the own-situation material toward T1 and T6 and toward adult children with a difficult or abusive parent.

videos.title: 10 Things to NEVER Do as a Dementia Caregiver
videos.how_counted: Hand tally; comments that only say thank you, praise the host, complain about the phrase 'care partners', or give tips to others were excluded. Many commenters ask 'what do I do when...' questions that describe their own situation, and those were counted. Approximate (+/- 15%).
videos.audience_note: A coaching-style video on dementia communication from a physician-coach whose replies often steer people to her paid academy and call booking. Commenters are mostly spouses and adult children currently living with dementia behavior, many newly diagnosed or recently bereaved, plus several people who have dementia themselves and some paid carers. The topic pulls strongly toward T9, T7 and T2, and toward questions about what to say in the moment; very little about money, paperwork or logistics.

videos.title: Why My Mom Lives in Memory Care | The Realities of Dementia Caregiving
videos.how_counted: Hand tally. About three quarters of the 500 threads are praise for the creator, 'you do not owe an explanation', prayers, or statements by facility workers, CNAs and nurses about their jobs. Counted only comments where the writer describes caring for or placing their own relative. Short 'I have been there' replies with no detail were counted in own_situation but not in theme counts. Approximate (+/- 20%).
videos.audience_note: A defensive video by a creator explaining why her mother with dementia lives in memory care, responding to people who questioned it. Commenters are mostly supporters, many of them nurses, CNAs and memory-care staff, and many family caregivers who also placed a relative and feel guilt or judgment. The topic pulls toward T1 (placement and cost), T9/T10 (violence, wandering) and T2 (guilt, exhaustion). Almost nothing about money systems, medications, doctors, long distance or paperwork.

new_themes.name: Caring for a parent who was abusive or neglectful earlier in life
new_themes.description: Many adult children say they must manage care for a parent who mistreated them, and that this adds resentment, guilt and a pull between duty and self-protection. Appears in all three videos, most in the money and dementia-tips videos.

example.quote: I still had to manage her care.

new_themes.name: Guilt and judgment about placing a relative in a facility
new_themes.description: Commenters describe stigma and criticism from others, and their own guilt, when a parent moves to memory care, and say they keep visiting daily to prove they have not abandoned the person. Specific to the memory-care video.

example.quote: It remains a stigma in our community to put our loved ones in residential care.

new_themes.name: Caregiver physically hurt or traumatized by the person with dementia
new_themes.description: Reports of being hit, kicked, threatened with knives, or having police called on the caregiver, with lasting fear or PTSD. Overlaps T9 and T10 but is about the caregiver's own safety and mental health.

example.quote: She's been in assisted living a month. I still have ptsd.

new_themes.name: Person in a facility begs to go home; visits become painful
new_themes.description: Family members describe visits where the relative in memory care or a nursing home cries and demands to go home, leaving the visitor unsure what to say or whether to visit less.

example.quote: Every time I go to visit which is everyday for a few hours all he wants to do is go home

new_themes.name: Who will care for the caregiver
new_themes.description: Older and sole caregivers worry that no one will be there for them, and some say they do not want their own children to go through caregiving; this also drives comments about saving, insurance, and ending one's own life rather than burden children.

example.quote: I often wonder who will be here for me when I need help.

new_themes.name: Care recipient resents lost control (driving, being helped)
new_themes.description: Caregivers describe taking away keys, insurance or independence behind the person's back, or the person resenting small acts of help, creating anger and guilt.

example.quote: He was furious with me. I did this behind his back.!

new_themes.name: People living with dementia comment themselves
new_themes.description: Several commenters on the dementia-tips video say they have just been diagnosed with early dementia and that a relative or in-law has become their caregiver, a perspective absent from the other videos.

example.quote: I will not stick around for the later stages.

caveats: Comments react to a video, so topic and creator shape who writes: the money video draws cost shock and many non-caregiver opinions, the dementia-tips video draws people asking in-the-moment behavior questions (and some replies come from the creator's coaching funnel), and the memory-care video draws supporters, facility staff and caregivers who already placed a relative, so T1 and T10 are over-represented there and T4, T5, T6 and T12 are under-represented. Counts are hand tallies and approximate; saved threads are a subset of all comments. Several quoted commenters are caring for a spouse, grandparent, aunt or in-law rather than a parent. A few quotes come from people who are paid workers or who are the person with dementia; these were used only where they illustrate a gap or new theme, and own-situation counts exclude non-family staff. No names are included. Some quotes are fragments of a longer comment and begin or end mid-sentence.
